LESSON: READING 2.2.1 READING FLUENCY

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.2: Reading 2.2.1 Reading Fluency
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 2.2.1 Reading Fluency, part of Strand 2 in Grade 6 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to read fluently? 2. How can one conserve the environment?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. brainstorm the meaning of intonation with peers,

2. listen to an audio recording based on the theme and identify instances of pauses,

3. collaborate with peers to search for texts from print and non-print sources on the theme and read,

4. work jointly with peers to practice reading with correct intonation and pause,

5. role play a news item bulletin based on the theme using the right intonation. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. brainstorm the meaning of intonation with peers,
2. listen to an audio recording based on the theme and identify instances of pauses,
3. collaborate with peers to search for texts from print and non-print sources on the theme and read,
4. work jointly with peers to practice reading with correct intonation and pause,
5. role play a news item bulletin based on the theme using the right intonation. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 2.2.1 Reading Fluency together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: This is enhanced as the learner engages actively to read texts about the theme with

correct intonation and pause.

● Learning to Learn: This is enhanced as the learner plans and manages time effectively when role playing a news item

bulletin based on the theme using the right intonation.

10

Values:
● Responsibility: The learner performs tasks assigned to them diligently as they collaborate with peers to search for texts

from print and non-print sources on the theme.

● Love: This is enhanced as the learner exhibits a caring attitude when brainstorming the meaning of intonation with

peers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Safety and security: This is promoted as the learner interacts with information about environmental conservation.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept on environmental conservation to similar content on the environment in Social

studies.
